purpose: Bounded Raft append network/disk overlap with existing durability proofs. Component qualification and remaining gaps; no complete optimization or release acceptance.
behavior: Only ordinary Ready messages consisting entirely of MsgAppend may overlap local persistence; snapshots and changed term/vote do not qualify.
The exact persistence ticket must first enter the existing bounded log-worker queue. Atomic admission is not a sync receipt or application/output proof.
Only eligible histories in the current physical batch join the existing fair runnable queue. Waiting groups stop being scheduled after append output drains.

Persisted follower responses, read states, applied publication, SDK receipts and required S3 coverage retain their existing proof gates. No fsync, owner/epoch check or acknowledgement requirement is removed.
Worker counts, admission banks, request deadlines and original service resources are unchanged. No wire/persisted format marker changes.

matched_owner_regression.scope: Real RF3/one group/three engines. Leader held sync overlaps actual peer disk appends; follower replies and leader publication stay fenced, image reopens exactly, and cancelled waiter retains physical ownership. Baseline follower/restart controls run after releasing its leader sync because no append is available early. No end-to-end throughput/latency, constrained Colima or full OPT/CG acceptance claim.

retention.scope: Concrete synthetic InMemory bytes after SQL/KV binding and Queue scenario cleanup, including successful fault controls. Opaque keys stay in private manifests; filenames are ordinals. Original operation failures survive export. These copies are nontransactional diagnostics, never recovery/admission proof. External stores cannot enter the typed helper.

Later independent cohorts cannot repair that old history. No failed history is reset or mutation reissued.
retention.unit_media_limit: Terminal file manifests describe remaining retained files; individual successful unit fixtures can clean their own temporary data.

recovery_gap.scope: The close report failed its complete-prefix assertion. No data-loss claim or causal link to the append pipeline is established. Current-source full recovery/disaster acceptance remains open.

original_comparison.required_profile: Three Colima nodes, each 1 vCPU/2 GiB; RF3/three cell groups; original shared RustFS. SQL/KV/Queue x Quorum/Quorum+S3/Fleet/Bucket x C1/4/16; 256-byte values; Queue batch eight; reversed repetitions; original 60-second windows.
original_comparison.actions: Read-only original-container inspection and df; no resource, volume, disk, compression, reserve, restart or data change.

P0: Complete recovery shutdown prefix and fenced recovery; current-source SDK/routing/read-refusal, historical/large/streaming KV availability, Python/lifecycle/release and full backend-fault qualification.

P1: Full OPT-01 through OPT-08: measured scheduling fairness, persistence/ReadIndex/archive batching, physical shared-file reclamation and once-only credit, reserve-aware placement and interrupted lifecycle.

limits: Qualification wall times include compilation, startup, deliberate fault holds and cleanup; they are not business request latency.
Controlled host-native RF3 mechanism tests do not establish constrained throughput, latency percentiles, a speedup ratio or a Fleet/Bucket comparison.

Ordinary/Axum SQL and KV, ordinary Queue callbacks, both Queue operator controls, long-callback/cross-deployment controls and discovery pass in the selected primitive run. Four Queue load cases still fail. A new successful cohort does not resolve an older ambiguous history.
Broader managed/disaster results remain at their own source pins. No complete OPT, CG, SDK, release or original performance gate is accepted.
